To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the bilingual approach is the most common in current literature and that (b) there are different perspectives about reading in deaf people, one of which advocates for the learning of Spanish as a second language only in written form, without the participation of oral language, and another that, on the contrary, considers that Spanish oral makes it easier to learn to read in a second language.

bilingualism is nowadays the main school of thoughts about reading processes in deaf students, and that, inside it, there are different ideas: one of these ideas is about the learning of Spanish only as a written language, without oral language, and another one is about the oral Spanish that makes it easier to learn reading and writing in that language.
the acquisition of the Spanish as second language is a very important aspect for the development of the deaf community, since it allows them to have a full access to knowledge.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the theoretical and empirical contributions about reading processes in deaf students, their difficulties, advances and educational practices, as well as the implications of the different approaches to bilingualism in the development of reading skills in this population.
the development of reading in deaf students and the different theories that have been developed to improve it.
the reading processes in the Spanish context, and the bilingual perspective, in which we have identified different ideas and theories, and the educational practices derived from these ideas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reading process in Spanish language by deaf people in bilingually contexts, is a complex task that needs a systematic and comprehensive training in order to achieve the best results.

bilingualism, as the main school of thoughts, is not the most effective one to learn Spanish as a foreigner language, and that the logogenia is not the best alternative method to develop syntaxes skills for deaf people.
bilingualism is the most important theory about reading in deaf people nowadays, but it is not enough to develop reading and writing skills in deaf people.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we think that the reading process in deaf people has a different development from the one of hearing people.
bilingualism is the most common approach in the current research and that there are different theories about reading in this approach.
the bilingualism is a good way to develop reading skills, but it should be trained more carefully and in a systematic way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
deaf people have to learn to read and write Spanish, so they can have a better and more complete acquisition of scholar knowledge.
deaf children should be taught to read and write Spanish as early as possible.

the bilingualism approach should be improved by the inclusion of more exercises and activities that would help to develop the skills needed to acquire the language, such as the phonological consciousness (visual variant) and the syntax.
